newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian defence minister told to quit military.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence minister told to quit military.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday ordered Defence Minister Igor Rodionov to quit the armed forces, but said he would remain Russian defence minister, the Kremlin said.

Yeltsin's order apparently creates Russia's first civilian defence minister. Rodionov, who has the rank of army general, turned 60 on December 1, which means he must retire from the military or his service must be extended by presidential decree.

Rodionov was named defence minister in July this year after Yeltsin sacked the hawkish and unpopular Pavel Grachev. Rodionov was strongly backed at the time by outspoken General Alexander Lebed, sacked by Yeltsin as Russia's security chief in October.
Rodionov is respected in the armed forces and has been acting to consolidate his grip over top brass in order to push ahead with the complicated task of military reform.
But he clashed with the Kremlin earlier this month when he apparently jumped the gun and announced that land forces commander General Vladimir Semyonov was being sacked for major violations.
The Kremlin said Yeltsin had agreed to dismiss Semyonov but had not done so yet.
